findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding the lock
findings.body: BuildIndex now writes b.cache under cacheMu, but TotalDocs (called from searchSupport.init logging) ranges over b.cache with no read lock. Concurrent builds during init (errgroup with multiple workers) can cause a concurrent map read/write, which is a fatal runtime error in Go. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock().

findings.title: Removing the whole-function lock allows duplicate index creation for the same key
findings.body: The lock previously serialized BuildIndex, which also prevented two concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource from both calling bleve.New on the same directory / overwriting each other. With the lock removed, getOrCreateIndex (GetIndex returns nil, then build) can run concurrently for the same key from Search and handleEvent, leading to two bleve indexes opened on the same file path (bleve.New fails with 'index already exists' or corrupts state) and one index silently replacing the other in the cache. The PR narrows the lock to only the map write, which does not protect this path.

findings.title: Eager Init in constructor makes startup failures fatal and can block/crash the process
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) which runs lifecycle init, the full search index build over all resources, and starts the watcher. Any error (e.g. DB not ready, index build failure) now causes the constructor to fail, and the index build runs synchronously with no timeout before the server is returned. The PR's own reviewer note asks what this could break; callers of NewResourceServer (module wiring, tests) must now tolerate long blocking startup and a hard failure. Also the ctx used is the server's internal background-derived context, so no caller cancellation applies.

findings.title: Stop() overwrites initErr and Init's once guard hides subsequent failures
findings.body: Init uses sync.Once and stores the error in s.initErr; Stop sets s.initErr to a 'stopping' error. Since Init is no longer called on each RPC, a failed init is only reported once from the constructor, and any caller that later calls Init gets a stale or misleading error. Combined with removing the per-RPC Init checks, a server whose init partly failed (e.g. lifecycle ok, search failed) silently serves requests with no index or no watcher.

findings.title: History, Origin and Search dereference nil search support
findings.body: After removing the Init guard, History and Origin call s.search.History / s.search.Origin directly. When search is not configured (opts.Search.Resources == nil or Backend nil, so s.search is nil), these methods panic with a nil pointer dereference. Previously the nil Init path did not guard this either, but Search has an explicit nil check while History/Origin do not.

findings.title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err in init goroutines
findings.body: Inside group.Go closures, totalBatchesIndexed++ is written concurrently by multiple goroutines without synchronization, and the shared outer variable err is assigned from concurrent goroutines (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`). This is a data race; the err assignment can also return the wrong error. Use a local error variable and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Watch context is detached from the init trace context and goroutine loops forever on channel close
findings.body: The watcher goroutine loops `v := <-events` without handling a closed channel; when the poller exits (closed stream), v becomes nil and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type, panicking. Also the watch context is context.Background() so it is never cancelled on server Stop, leaking the goroutine.

findings.title: No tests cover the new eager initialization or the lock change
findings.body: The behavioral change (init moved into constructor, per-RPC Init removed, locking changed in BuildIndex) has no accompanying unit test for concurrent BuildIndex or for NewResourceServer returning an error when init fails. The module server test change only adds a skip for postgres, which does not validate any of the changes.
